newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Reborn Indonesia paper aims for regional role.
newsitem.headline: Reborn Indonesia paper aims for regional role.

text.p: A prominent Indonesian businessman relaunched the country's oldest English language daily on Wednesday pledging to create a regional newspaper.

Media tycoon Peter Gontha relaunched the 42-year-old Indonesian Observer promising independent reporting on business and economic news not covered by two other local English-language papers or the regional dailies available in Indonesia.

"The Indonesian Observer will be as independent as any other newspaper. I have been very much for openness and the democracy of the press," said Gontha, a founder of the first nightly non-government television news broadcast on the privately-owned RCTI station.
"We will be within the rules and regulations. We probably will be more free than the press in Singapore, that's for sure, in openness and how we will be reporting things," he told a media conference.

The Observer plans to boost its circulation to 24,000 copies a day from the current 5,000 by targeting local professionals and expatriates in Indonesia as well as readers in Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and Hong Kong.
"We are not trying to compete with any other newspaper, what we are trying to do here is to be complementary to the newspapers and the media that are already available," he said.
